title: `SafeTransferLib` return-data check accepts tokens that return garbage in the first word when `returndatasize > 31` but value ≠ 1 — actually rejects valid tokens returning >32 bytes, and accepts tokens returning exactly `1` in 32 bytes only; more importantly, **fee-on-transfer and false-returning tokens are not detectable**
impact: `safeTransfer`/`safeTransferFrom` only verify the call didn't revert and the return convention is plausible. They do **not** verify the received amount. Integrations (vaults, routers) that assume `amount` arrived in full will accrue accounting drift with fee-on-transfer/rebasing tokens (USDT-like deflationary tokens, stETH-style rebasers), enabling share-price manipulation in downstream ERC4626-style vaults (donation/inflation via understated deposits).
